"Implement the solution in src/lib.rs so that the tests in tests/fizzy.rs pass. The specification follows.

# Description

FizzBuzz is a children's game of counting through the integers. For each of them, if it's divisible by three, substitute the word \"fizz\"; if divisible by five, substitute \"buzz\"; if both, say both; if neither, say the number. It is not particularly difficult to implement, though it enjoyed some popularity for a time as [a quick way to tell whether entry-level programming applicants knew how to program _at all_](https://blog.codinghorror.com/why-cant-programmers-program/).

It has since fallen somewhat into disfavor for that task, because applicants began memorizing FizzBuzz implementations instead of learning to program.

We're going to do something more interesting than the basics: your task in this exercise is to implement FizzBuzz:

- with fully-customizable rules about what numbers produce what words
- fully generic on a very restricted minimal trait set
- such that it works just as well for the Collatz Sequence as for steadily increasing numbers
- with convenient helpers to make its use ergonomic


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper modules may go under src/; you may add [dependencies] from the offline crates listed in OFFLINE_CRATES.md to Cargo.toml."

## Summary

I implemented the FizzBuzz solution in `src/lib.rs`. The design:

- **`Matcher<T>`** — holds a `Box<dyn Fn(T) -> bool>` predicate and a `String` substitution. `Matcher::new` takes any `Fn(T) -> bool + 'static` closure and any `Into<String>` substitution, so it works for the by-value closures used in the `custom` test.

- **`Fizzy<T>`** — a `Vec<Matcher<T>>`. `new()` and `add_matcher(self, ...)` are bound-free and chainable; `apply(iter)` maps each element through all matchers in order, concatenating matching substitutions, and falls back to `n.to_string()` when nothing matched. It only requires `T: Display + Copy` (Copy because the by-value matchers consume the element and we reuse it afterward).

- **`fizz_buzz<T>()`** — a convenience constructor requiring the minimal set `T: Display + Copy + Rem<Output = T> + From<u8> + PartialEq`. It uses `n % 3.into() == 0.into()` so the `3`/`0` literals are converted into `T` via `From<u8>` — this is what lets it work uniformly for `i32`, `u8`, `u64`, `f64`, and the custom `Fizzable` type in the `minimal_generic_bounds` test.

The key to satisfying the spec's "fully generic on a very restricted minimal trait set" is that `Rem<Output = T>` + `From<u8>` + `PartialEq` are enough to express divisibility without assuming any specific numeric type, and `apply` only needs `Display + Copy`, so it works for any iterator of `T` — sequential ranges, the Collatz sequence, or float `successors`.

I did not modify the tests or build files, and no external dependencies were needed.
